textChars._of: the taught topics — the shape a question set is written to

_note: 2026-08-12: the whole book ships. Parts I (sounds), IV (word formation)
and VI (prosody) used to be dropped, along with 12 sections behind a
heading the parser read as structural — §12 'A Noun is the name of a
person, place, thing, or quality' among them. All of it was dropped for
one reason, that none of it can carry an English->Latin translation, and
that is a fact about questions rather than about reading. So it is now
shipped as 35 topics marked `readingOnly`: read and paged through like any
other page, never studied, and not counted in anybody's progress.
Nothing already here moved. The 114 taught topics have the same ids, the
same titles, the same refs, the same families and byte-identical text; no
test file was orphaned and no progress migrated. `assigned` 325 -> 376 and
`dropped` 51 -> 0, because those 51 sections became topics rather than
because anything new was found. rowShapedLines 1921 -> 2034 and
tableRowsRecovered 2098 -> 2212 are the tables in the new parts: Part I's
vowel tables and Part VI's metrical schemes had never been through G6.
textChars are unchanged, being of the taught topics alone — the shape a
question set is written to, which averaging in a page of prosody would
measure neither of.
Six of these numbers were already stale when the 2026-08-05 rebuild
remeasured them — median 1773 -> 1803, p90 6008 -> 6010, max 17786 ->
17790, rowShapedLines 1911 -> 1921, tableRowsRecovered 2103 -> 2098,
romanPoints 10 -> 9. Nothing in that rebuild touches the grammar, and
content/ and the built bundle report the same figures, so this is the
record catching up with a parse it had already been given.
The parser moved from Gutenberg's plain text to its HTML on 2026-07-30.
Every number here moved with it, and none of the movements is a loss:
topics 135 -> 114. The plain-text parser opened a topic wherever it took a
paradigm caption for a run-heading, so amō and amor were two topics and the
six irregular verbs were six. The HTML has real headings, so those runs sit
under the heading the book gave them. No section became unreachable —
`assigned` went up, not down.
sourceSections 371 -> 376. The old reader required section numbers to run
strictly +1 and lost §372-375 (prosody, dropped either way) plus §222A.
textChars are measured on the words: the inline emphasis markup is stripped
before counting (see core's plainText). The median rose because whole
table cells now arrive whole, where the plain text truncated them at the
column edge and left the remainder as a loose line.
rowShapedLines 2015 -> 1911 with tableRowsRecovered 2052 -> 2103: fewer
lines carrying more rows, which is the wrapped-cell bug being fixed. A
cell that used to wrap over three physical lines is now one row.

_comment: The pack's further grammars, one entry apiece. Bennett is above, because
he is the syllabus the app teaches; these are gated to the same standard
and read by nothing at runtime yet.

lane.book: Lane, A Latin Grammar for Schools and Colleges (1898)

_note: What the crosswalk carries, not what Lane was written for: Lane's
topics are served out of the questions written against Bennett, so
a Lane topic no table row reaches has nothing to teach from.
235 topics and 6,025 questions until 2026-08-12, when the table was
extended over the 220 topics the quotation run never asked about —
it covered §1056-2421 because that is where Lane prints the sentences
it was walking. 196 of the 220 were placed, 24 had no counterpart.
The declensions and conjugations are the part with a knowable answer
and every one of them is right: stems in -ā-, -o-, -u-, -ē- onto the
first, second, fourth and fifth, the consonant and -i- stems onto the
third, and -āre/-ēre/-ere/-īre onto the four conjugations.
13 Bennett topics stay unreachable. Seven are word-order and style,
which Lane has no chapter on. The other six are ones Bennett isolates
and Lane folds into a neighbour: Lane's conjunctions went to Bennett's
Coordinate Conjunctions rather than his list of the forms, and its
Wish to the Optative rather than the Volitive Subjunctive. Both are
the books disagreeing, which is what a second grammar is for.
First measured 2026-08-11, the commit that wrote lane-parse.py.
Only maxTopics needed a threshold of its own (300-600, against Bennett's
60-300). Every other gate Bennett was calibrated at, Lane clears
unchanged — which is the finding, not a coincidence: the two books
disagree about how many topics a grammar has, and agree about how long
one should be.
2026-08-12: the whole book ships. The 714 sections that used to be
dropped — §§1-396 (parts of speech, sound, word formation) and
§§2428-2739 (prosody and versification) — are now 209 topics marked
`readingOnly`, read like any other page and studied like none. That is
37% of Lane's text, which was the largest hole in either pack. maxTopics
went 600 -> 800 to hold them; nothing else about the shape moved, and
textChars is unchanged because it is of the taught topics alone.
Six sections stay dropped and are the only ones in either pack: §§2740-
2745, Lane's key to the authors he cites, of which §2745 alone is 317,000
characters of 'Ter. = Terentius'. It is apparatus rather than grammar —
the same thing Bennett's parser has always refused at INDEX OF THE
SOURCES — and it is keyed on the heading rather than the number, so a
Gutenberg re-release cannot renumber it back in. G10 exists to say that
nothing else is ever dropped.
No taught topic moved: the same 459 ids, titles, refs and families, and
byte-identical text but for ln-2424-expression-of-fractions, whose group
always ran to §2428 and was cut at §2427 by the old range filter. Its ref
is now 2424-2428. To keep those ids fixed the titler runs the syllabus
first and the reading pages second: Lane heads a chapter of word
formation 'Denominatives' exactly as it heads §839, and naming them in
one pass would have renamed §839 and orphaned its questions.
rowShapedLines 1364 -> 1728 and tableRowsRecovered 1462 -> 1826 are the
tables in the new parts. G9 has not been read through.

_quotedNote: 2,409 of these questions have an answer somebody wrote, over 91 topics of
114 — 889 over 50 before the Lane run, 2,387 over 62 after it, and 91 once
the pools were dealt again on 2026-08-12. The pools did not grow. What
changed is that a sentence can now reach a topic two ways rather than one.
Until now `topics` on a pool record was a model's answer and nothing else,
filed per sentence by build-quote-pool.mjs or per source section by the two
grammar readers. That is the only kind of answer syntax admits. It left the
inflection families at nothing — 8 of 9 noun topics, 14 of 17 verb-forms —
because no grammarian's syntax section illustrates the fourth declension.
inflection-topics.mjs adds the topics a LOOKUP confirms, out of
grammar/inflection-topics.tsv, whose every row carries the sentence of
Bennett's that licenses it. It calls no model: a lemma's declension and
conjugation are fields of lemmas.json.gz and the cell a form fills is a row
of paradigms.txt.gz. 2,421 of the 2,507 pool records were filed under at
least one inflection topic they had not been filed under before.
Three rules keep it honest, and the third is the one worth keeping. A form
licenses a class only when EVERY candidate lemma of it agrees — one reading
the table cannot classify and the token is refused, which is what stops `dī`
being filed under the fifth declension. A declension wants an oblique cell,
because a nominative singular shows a word and not a paradigm. And a rule
that licenses nothing was withdrawn rather than loosened: the relative and
interrogative pronouns share almost every form, so no sentence proves which
is meant. `impersonal` went the same way — wiktextract writes it on a sense,
so it marks cadō, and 276 quotations were filed under §138 on the strength
of `cadunt` before Bennett's own list replaced it.
Nothing was created. quote-tests --allocate --per-topic 16 deals the whole
pool at once, sparsest topic first, out of the surplus of the topics that
have most and never below a donor floor of 16. Conditional sentences went
255 -> 105 quoted questions, temporal clauses 227 -> 103, moods in dependent
clauses 202 -> 100 — 25 topics gave up something, none below 92 — and about
thirty topics that had nothing got sixteen. A sentence still ships once, so
answerKey means what it says and C4 is unmoved at 4 duplicate prompts.
Attested share by family: verb-syntax 36%, noun-syntax 35%, adj-pron-syntax
35%, particles 30%, pron 24%, style 17%, nouns 15%, adj 13%, verb-forms 13%.
The four inflection families were at 1-2% and are the whole of the delta.
23 topics still ship none, and they are the ones no lookup can reach: the
style family and word-order, the umbrella topics whose children carry the
belongs to the lemma rather than to the sentence, and §89 on the relative
pronoun. Those wait for another book, not for a looser rule.
answerTokens 65,132 -> 65,323 and dictResolvedPct held at 99.1. E1 and E2
did not move: 105 unattested tokens, 89 distinct, worst question 2. Nothing
here could have moved them — the pools were filtered with the same
classifier when they were built, and this deals them rather than adding any.
_note: Three backfill runs took the syllabus from 1,088 tests to 1,722, and every
topic is at or above its size-scaled target. The gap the coverage report
was built to expose is closed.
The 2026-07-30 reparse regrouped the syllabus, so 27 topics' tests were
carried onto the topic that now covers their sections (see
scripts/remap-tests.mjs). Nothing was regenerated and nothing was thrown
away — hence max 26 -> 63 tests on a topic, which is six merged paradigm
topics' worth of drills under one heading. Only §313, which the old
parser had swallowed into Conditional Sentences, was newly generated.
keptRatioPct covers two of the three backfill runs. gen-stats.json is
written when a run finishes, and the middle run was stopped by hand before
it wrote anything, so roughly 270 shipped tests have no rejection-rate
data. C6 reads green on what it can see, not on everything.

_formKeysNote: 893,854 -> 973,267 when build-lemmas started attaching a wordform
entry's forms to the ranked lemma it says it is a form of. Wiktionary
gives a Latin participle its own entry and its own declension and leaves
the parent verb listing the citation form alone, so capiō — rank 245 —
shipped without captūrōs or any other form of its own future participle.
Note that no lemma was added: 55,312 before and after. The forms were
always the forms of a word the corpus counted; nothing could find them.
The count only moved once --max-rank 20000 was passed. The script's
default of 7000 does not reproduce what this pack ships and rebuilding
at it silently drops ranks 7001-19342 — 712 answer tokens' worth of
_note: Rebuilt on 2026-08-06, and this is the first record of a pack that ships
the whole dictionary rather than a corpus's vocabulary.
The word that caused it was `reste`. It is the ablative of `restis`,
rope; Wiktionary has it; the app said it was not in the dictionary. The
cause was never a rank cutoff — --max-rank was already past the end of
the list — but the list itself: build-lemmas walked ranked lemmas only,
and Latin's frequency list is seven works long. Apicius, Augustine,
Caesar, Catullus, Cicero, Ovid and Seneca between them never needed a
rope, so `restis` had no rank and was never visited.
distinctLemmas 19,292 -> 55,312, formKeys 491,398 -> 893,854. The tail
is every lemma entry the dictionary holds that the ranked half missed:
36,021 of them, unranked on purpose. Of the reference's 885,996 entries
only 52,424 are lemmas at all — the other 833,572 are wordform entries
(`amābam` as its own row), already reachable through the forms table of
the entry they point at, and shipping them would have multiplied the
file to add nothing.
The two mean-gloss figures are the point of the split. A ranked word is
one the student will meet again and gets six senses; a tail word is one
they are checking once and gets two, capped at 140 characters. Six for
everything would have cost about 2 MB on a phone to say more about
words nobody is learning.
nounGenderPct 99.2 -> 98.7 and meanGlossChars 72 -> 47 are both the tail
arriving, not a regression: the ranked half still reads 59 characters a
gloss, and the tail is thinner because it was written to be.
packResolvedPct is unchanged at 99.3 by construction. `attests` now asks
for a *ranked* record rather than merely a key, so C5 and gen-tests's
ok/unverified classifier are exactly as strict as they were when the map
held ranked lemmas alone. Shipping the tail widens what a student can
look up and nothing else.
_fieldsNote: Lemma records gained `conjugation` (6,257 verbs) and `tags` (579 deponents)
on 2026-08-12, both read from the same wiktextract sense tags `declension`
already came from. A verb's `declension` is its participle's and says
nothing about how it conjugates; the two are read separately for that
reason. Nothing else in the table moved — a --verify rebuild reproduced
100.00% of the shipped form keys, and only these two fields differ.

_note: 305 -> 105 unattested tokens: 38 the enclitic on marīque and trēsve, 23
mid-sentence proper nouns the checker now exempts as the generator
always did, and 139 from build-lemmas learning to attach a participle's
declension to its parent verb.
What is left is not invented Latin. It is archaic gerundives (capiundae,
potiundī), -ier passive infinitives (aperīrier, mūnīrier), -ībam
imperfects (audībam, nescībam), regular comparatives no dictionary
enumerates, and sentence-initial proper nouns. Every one of the archaisms
sits in bn-116 peculiarities-of-conjugation or bn-338 the-gerund — the
topics that exist to teach exactly that form. Regenerating them would
make E2 greener and the pack less true, so the budget records them
instead. It is 105, and it has no headroom on purpose: the next run that
writes a form the reference cannot confirm has to raise it deliberately
and say which questions bought the increase.
71 more tokens are in reference/dictionary.db and not in what the pack
ships. They are a thin index rather than a bad sentence; closing that gap
is a build-lemmas job and touches no question.
The dictionary went from 2.1 MB to 4.2 MB across its two files when the
tail went in. Neither is precached, so what the study loop costs on a
plane is unchanged at ~427 KB; what moved is the one-time fetch the
vocabulary feature makes, and the screens that warn about it now read
their figure from the built files rather than from a number typed by
hand (see __DICTIONARY_BYTES__).
content/ is written in the same split shape the bundle is — a lemma
table plus a sorted form index — so build-web-content copies it through
rather than splitting it. The old denormalized map repeated a gloss
under every form and inflated to 116 MB for a third of these words; at
this size it would have been some 300 MB, which is more than apps/cli
could parse.
